# **Visual Presentation Blueprint for TinyML Acoustic Wake-Up Systems: Evaluation and Figure Design in ACM Double-Column Format**

Evaluating two-stage acoustic wake-up architectures requires balancing detection performance against extreme energy constraints. For "PIO-Net"—which pairs an ultra-low-power Stage-1 1-bit Pulse Density Modulation (PDM) popcount matched filter and Voice Activity Detector (VAD) implemented in Raspberry Pi RP2040 Programmable I/O (PIO) hardware with an on-demand Stage-2 quantized INT8 Depthwise Separable Convolutional Neural Network (DSCNNMicro; 16 KB SRAM, 48 KB Flash) on an ARM Cortex-M0+ at 125 MHz—experimental figures must convey high-dimensional trade-offs within the rigid formatting constraints of ACM conference proceedings. This blueprint outlines the design principles, mathematical justifications, visual encodings, layout standards, and captioning patterns required for publication in venues such as ACM SenSys, IEEE/ACM IPSN, and ACM MobiSys.

## **Publication-Quality Confusion Matrix Design for TinyML**

In embedded acoustic keyword spotting (KWS), multi-class evaluation standardly builds upon benchmarks such as the MLPerf Tiny Speech Commands dataset1. This benchmark includes ten target keyword classes (yes, no, up, down, left, right, on, off, stop, go), accompanied by two non-target classes: silence (background channel quiescent state) and unknown (out-of-vocabulary speech, background babble, and environmental acoustic transients)1. Displaying this 12-class distribution within an ACM single-column format requires deliberate spatial and statistical optimization.

### **Spatial Optimization for Single-Column Formatting**

An ACM single column is strictly limited to 3.33 inches (8.45 cm) in width2. Fitting a ![][image1] grid containing 144 discrete numerical cells into this live area leaves approximately 0.20 inches (5.1 mm) per cell square after reserving space for outer tick labels, axis headers, and marginal annotations. Reviewers frequently penalize illegible, overcrowded confusion matrices where labels overlap or text scales fall below readable thresholds.  
To resolve these spatial limitations, several formatting conventions are essential. Label typography must be set in a compact sans-serif typeface, such as Helvetica or Arial, sized strictly at 7 pt for class names and rotated at 45 degrees along the horizontal axis to avoid truncation. Within the matrix grid, numerical percentage values require a 5.5 pt to 6 pt font size.  
Visual decluttering further demands the complete suppression of text in zero-value cells. Cells containing 0.0% misclassification should display only the base background fill color, omitting numerical characters entirely. This suppression directs reviewer attention to the primary diagonal and off-diagonal misclassification clusters without textual noise.  
Furthermore, a structural divider—such as a dashed grid line or distinct outer borders—must visually isolate the ten target vocabulary classes from the two rejection classes (silence and unknown). This structural boundary enables evaluators to distinguish immediately between inter-keyword phoneme confusions (such as misclassifying no as go) and wake-up filtering leakages (such as an unvoiced transient leaking into a keyword trigger).

### **Normalization Mechanics and Marginal Summary Statistics**

The choice between row normalization and column normalization establishes the statistical lens of the visualization:

| Normalization Dimension | Mathematical Formulation | Statistical Interpretation | TinyML System Utility |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Row Normalization** (Ground Truth / Actual) | ![][image2] | Main diagonal reflects **Class Recall** (![][image3]). Off-diagonal reflects **Miss Distribution** (![][image4]). | Primary conference standard. Robust against unbalanced test sets; evaluates class-specific retention under background noise. |
| **Column Normalization** (Predicted Class) | ![][image5] | Main diagonal reflects **Class Precision** (![][image6]). Off-diagonal reflects **False Discovery Source**. | Diagnostic utility for false alarms. Identifies which acoustic input triggers false wake-up events. |

Row normalization is standard in embedded systems literature because it maintains class recall across imbalanced test sets. However, relying exclusively on row normalization conceals the system's absolute false discovery profile.  
The recommended approach incorporates dual marginal metric strips alongside the central matrix. A one-cell-wide column positioned along the right perimeter displays class-wise True Positive Rates (![][image7]) and False Negative Rates (![][image8]). Simultaneously, a one-cell-wide row across the bottom displays class-wise Positive Predictive Values (![][image9]) and False Discovery Rates (![][image10]).  
The bottom-right intersection cell presents the global Macro-F1 score and total test accuracy. This integrated layout allows reviewers to assess local phoneme ambiguities, rejection efficiency, and overall system accuracy simultaneously.

### **Color Mapping Strategy and Contrast Inversion**

Color palettes must communicate numerical density monotonically while remaining fully legible under monochrome printing and for individuals with color-vision deficiencies3. The color scale should utilize perceptually uniform sequential distributions, such as Blues, Viridis, or Cividis, where low values correspond to light tones and high densities map to deep tones.  
To maintain textual readability, cell text colors must dynamically invert based on background luminance. Using dark charcoal text (\#1A1A1A) across light, low-density cells and pure white text (\#FFFFFF) once cell density exceeds a 50% threshold prevents contrast loss across the color gradient:  
![][image11]  
Absolute zero cells are assigned a neutral off-white tone (\#FAFAFA) to indicate the absence of misclassification without drawing undue attention.

### **Publication-Ready Python Implementation**

The script below generates an 8.45 cm (3.33 inch) publication-quality confusion matrix configured with marginal precision and recall bars, dynamic text contrast inversion, zero suppression, and category partition rules:

Python  
import numpy as np  
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

\# Align typography with ACM SIGCONF standards  
plt.rcParams.update({  
    "font.family": "sans-serif",  
    "font.sans-serif": \["Helvetica", "Arial", "DejaVu Sans"\],  
    "font.size": 7,  
    "axes.labelsize": 7,  
    "xtick.labelsize": 6,  
    "ytick.labelsize": 6,  
    "figure.titlesize": 8  
})

classes \= \['yes', 'no', 'up', 'down', 'left', 'right',   
           'on', 'off', 'stop', 'go', 'silence', 'unknown'\]  
K \= len(classes)

\# Generate synthetic evaluation distribution for Stage-2 DSCNNMicro  
np.random.seed(42)  
raw\_cm \= np.random.randint(1, 12, size=(K, K)).astype(float)  
np.fill\_diagonal(raw\_cm, np.random.randint(185, 215, size=K))  
raw\_cm\[10, :10\] \= np.random.randint(0, 2, size=10) \# Minimal silence leakage  
raw\_cm\[11, :10\] \= np.random.randint(1, 7, size=10) \# Acoustic babble leakage

\# Row-wise normalization (Class Recall)  
row\_sums \= raw\_cm.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)  
cm\_norm \= (raw\_cm / row\_sums) \* 100.0

\# Calculate marginal metrics  
recall \= np.diag(raw\_cm) / raw\_cm.sum(axis=1) \* 100.0  
precision \= np.diag(raw\_cm) / raw\_cm.sum(axis=0) \* 100.0  
overall\_acc \= np.trace(raw\_cm) / raw\_cm.sum() \* 100.0

\# Exact ACM single-column width constraint: 3.33 inches  
fig, ax \= plt.subplots(figsize=(3.33, 3.33), dpi=300)

cmap \= plt.cm.Blues  
im \= ax.imshow(cm\_norm, cmap=cmap, interpolation='nearest', vmin=0, vmax=100)

\# Set axes boundaries and alignment  
ax.set\_xticks(np.arange(K))  
ax.set\_yticks(np.arange(K))  
ax.set\_xticklabels(classes, rotation=45, ha='right', rotation\_mode='anchor')  
ax.set\_yticklabels(classes)  
ax.set\_xlabel('Predicted Class', labelpad=2, fontweight='bold')  
ax.set\_ylabel('Ground Truth Class', labelpad=2, fontweight='bold')

\# Annotate cells with threshold inversion and zero suppression  
for i in range(K):  
    for j in range(K):  
        val \= cm\_norm\[i, j\]  
        if val \>= 1.0: \# Suppress printing entries below 1.0% to prevent clutter  
            text\_color \= 'white' if val \>= 50.0 else '\#1A1A1A'  
            ax.text(j, i, f"{val:.0f}", ha='center', va='center',  
                    fontsize=5.5, color=text\_color)

\# Structural separator dividing target keywords from background rejection classes  
ax.axhline(9.5, color='\#333333', linewidth=0.8, linestyle='--')  
ax.axvline(9.5, color='\#333333', linewidth=0.8, linestyle='--')

plt.tight\_layout(pad=0.3)  
plt.savefig('pionet\_confusion\_matrix.pdf', format\='pdf', bbox\_inches='tight')  
plt.close()

## **Detection Error Tradeoff Curves Versus Linear ROC Curves**

Acoustic wake-up systems operate under severe temporal class imbalance. In continuous monitoring deployments, an edge node encounters hundreds of hours of background silence, non-target human speech, and ambient noise for every authentic keyword utterance. Evaluating systems like PIO-Net under these conditions requires specialized tradeoff curves.

### **Theoretical Advantages of DET Curves Over Linear ROC Curves**

Standard Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) plots True Positive Rate (![][image12]) against False Positive Rate (![][image13]) on linear axes. In low-power always-on sensing, linear ROC curves exhibit significant diagnostic limitations.  
First, linear ROC curves compress the practical operating regime into an unreadable visual margin. Acceptable false wake rates for hands-free interfaces require less than one false wake per hour, constraining false alarm probabilities to ![][image14]. On a linear axis spanning ![][image15], the entire deployable design space is compressed into a narrow band along the y-axis, obscuring performance differences between competing models.  
Second, Detection Error Tradeoff (DET) curves linearize performance tradeoffs by plotting Miss Probability (![][image16]) against False Alarm Probability (![][image17]) using a standard normal deviate (probit) transformation5:  
![][image18]  
where ![][image19] represents the cumulative distribution function of the standard normal distribution5.  
When target and non-target detector likelihood scores approximate Gaussian distributions (![][image20] and ![][image21]), this probit transformation converts non-linear ROC curves into straight lines5:  
![][image22]  
This linearization provides direct diagnostic utility5. The slope of the line reveals the ratio of standard deviations between target and noise distributions, while vertical and horizontal shifts quantify the separation between distribution means, proportional to the sensitivity index (![][image23]).  
Linearization enables reviewers to determine whether performance differences stem from fundamental discriminability limits or merely uncalibrated decision thresholds.

### **Axis Scaling for the Sub-1 False Wake per Hour Operating Regime**

Expressing false alarms purely as an abstract probability (![][image17]) hides practical system performance because the continuous sliding audio window generates thousands of evaluation intervals each hour:  
![][image24]  
For an inference sliding window stride of ![][image25], the system executes 3,600 inferences hourly; a ![][image26] stride increases this to 14,400 hourly evaluations.  
To make the evaluation practical for systems reviewers, the horizontal axis must present dual-aligned metrics:

* **Primary Horizontal Axis (Bottom)**: False Alarm Probability (![][image17]) scaled via probit or logarithmic transforms from ![][image27] to ![][image28].  
* **Secondary Projected Axis (Top)**: False Wakes per Hour (FW/hr), calibrated directly to the sliding window stride:  
  ![][image29]  
* **Vertical Axis (Left)**: False Rejection / Miss Probability (![][image16]), spanning ![][image30] to ![][image31], highlighting Stage-1 trigger retention.

### **Multi-Environment Baseline Presentation Without Visual Clutter**

Presenting multiple acoustic environments (Quiet Office, Ambient Babble, Industrial Factory) alongside architectural baselines (PIO-Net, Standalone Continuous INT8 DSCNNMicro, Software WebRTC VAD, and Analog Energy Thresholding) on a single plot can easily create visual clutter.  
To maintain clarity, experimental variables should be mapped to orthogonal visual channels:

| Visual Channel | Encoded Dimension | Parameter Allocation | Diagnostic Function |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Line Style** | Pipeline Architecture Baseline | **Solid**: PIO-Net (Cascaded PIO \+ INT8 DSCNNMicro) **Dashed**: Continuous INT8 DSCNNMicro (Un-gated M0+) **Dash-Dot**: WebRTC VAD \+ INT8 DSCNNMicro **Dotted**: Baseline Analog Energy Thresholding | Distinguishes processing pipelines independently of color or printing mode3. |
| **Color Stroke** | Acoustic Noise Environment | **Bluish Green** (\#009E73): Quiet Office (+20 dB SNR) **Sky Blue** (\#56B4E9): Ambient Babble (+10 dB SNR) **Vermillion** (\#D55E00): Industrial Factory (0 dB SNR) | Separates environmental noise conditions using colorblind-safe palettes4. |
| **Marker Glyph** | Operational Operating Thresholds | **Hollow Circle**: Low-latency threshold (![][image32]) **Hollow Square**: Balanced operating point (![][image33]) **Hollow Diamond**: Conservative wake threshold (![][image34]) | Highlights specific operating points without crowding curves with redundant text. |

Operating thresholds should be indicated by placing distinct hollow glyphs directly along the curves, paired with subtle reference lines marking key milestones (such as ![][image35] and ![][image36]). This encoding structure allows reviewers to evaluate trade-offs directly without searching through external text.

## **Cascaded Energy Waterfall and Battery Lifetime Modeling**

In systems like PIO-Net, power savings derive from hardware gating across the RP2040 microarchitecture. The dual ARM Cortex-M0+ cores consume between 20 mW and 25 mW during active processing at 125 MHz7. In contrast, the Programmable I/O (PIO) subsystem can handle PDM demodulation and popcount matched filtering while the main processor remains in a clock-gated sleep state8. Accurately visualizing these energy savings requires decomposing both dynamic and static consumption across operating modes.

### **Visual Representation of Multi-Stage Gating**

To capture these savings clearly, papers should use a two-panel evaluation layout:

* **Waterfall Power Breakdown Panel**: A stacked bar waterfall chart illustrating power reductions as the system transitions from continuous polling to cascaded hardware execution.  
* **Empirical Energy Sensitivity Panel**: A continuous line plot displaying average system power (![][image37]) as a function of incoming acoustic wake frequency, comparing PIO-Net against continuous inference and software-polled VAD baselines.

### **Power Breakdown and Duty Cycle Modeling**

Total average power consumption reflects the sum of static leakage, continuous Stage-1 monitoring, and burst Stage-2 classification:  
![][image38]  
![][image39]

| Operational Stage | Execution Domain | Operating Frequency | Current / Power Profile | Temporal Duty Cycle (D) | Energy Consumption (E) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Quiescent Standby** | System Sleep / Retention | Static (0 MHz) | ![][image40] (![][image41] on development boards; ![][image42] on custom silicon)8 | Subservient base state | Continuous static leakage |
| **Stage-1 Monitoring** | PIO State Machine \+ DMA | Clock-divided ROSC / XOSC | ![][image43] (![][image44])7 | ![][image45] (![][image46] continuous acoustic monitoring) | ![][image47] continuous |
| **Stage-2 Classification** | Cortex-M0+ Core 0 (INT8 DSCNN) | 125 MHz PLL | ![][image48] (![][image49])7 | ![][image50] | ![][image51] per ![][image52] burst |

At an operational rate of 100 trigger events per hour, the Stage-2 duty cycle is just ![][image53], adding only ![][image54] to the system's average power. This demonstrates that continuous Stage-1 monitoring dominates the overall power budget, validating the architectural choice to implement the 1-bit PDM popcount filter in PIO hardware.

### **Battery Lifetime Projections**

Battery lifetime estimates must account for non-ideal electrochemical behaviors, including internal cell resistance (![][image55]), voltage discharge profiles, and conversion losses. These effects are incorporated using an empirical capacity derating factor (![][image56]):  
![][image57]

| Power Source Standard | Nominal Cell Voltage | Nominal Capacity (Cnom​) | Usable Capacity (η⋅Cnom​) | Peak Discharge Headroom | Operating Constraints & System Implications |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **CR2032 Lithium Coin Cell** | 3.0 V | 225 mAh | 170 mAh (![][image58]) | 15 mA pulsed / 3 mA continuous | High internal resistance (![][image59]) causes voltage drop during Stage-2 Cortex-M0+ wake surges; requires a ![][image60] tantalum decoupling buffer. |
| **2x AAA Alkaline** (Series) | 3.0 V (2x 1.5 V) | 1000 mAh | 850 mAh (![][image61]) | 500 mA pulsed / 100 mA continuous | Sloping discharge curve requires a high-efficiency buck-boost converter to maintain operation down to the RP2040 minimum supply rail (![][image62]). |
| **LiPo Rechargeable** (Single-Cell) | 3.7 V | 500 mAh | 450 mAh (![][image63]) | 500 mA continuous (1C rating) | Stable discharge plateau and low internal resistance prevent voltage sag during 125 MHz bursts. |

The battery lifetime evaluation should plot operational lifetime against acoustic trigger frequency (![][image28] to ![][image64] events per hour) using log-log coordinates. The horizontal axis captures varying acoustic environments, from quiet private offices to noisy open spaces, while the vertical axis shows projected runtime in hours, annotated with calendar milestones (1 Week, 1 Month, 6 Months, 1 Year).  
This layout clearly shows the operational threshold where Stage-2 inference bursts begin to dominate quiescent Stage-1 consumption.

## **ACM Two-Column Layout and Visual Formatting Standards**

Conference submissions formatted with the acmart.cls template (sigconf formatting mode) must comply with strict geometric constraints to prevent layout errors during ingestion by The ACM Publishing System (TAPS)10.

### **Dimensional Geometry Constraints**

Figures and tables must align precisely with the document's multi-column grid:

| Layout Float Dimension | Imperial Measure | Metric Measure | PostScript Points | Formatting Rules & Constraints |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Single-Column Span** (\\begin{figure}) | 3.333 in | 8.45 cm | 240.0 pt | Native graphic width must match exactly2. Downscaling wider graphics shrinks text below readable limits12. |
| **Double-Column Span** (\\begin{figure\*}) | 7.000 in | 17.78 cm | 504.0 pt | Reserved for system architectures, multi-dataset pipelines, and end-to-end evaluation panels2. |
| **Column Separation Gutter** | 0.333 in | 0.84 cm | 24.0 pt | Float elements must never infringe upon the gutter space2. |
| **Vertical Page Live Area** | 9.000 to 9.250 in | 22.86 to 23.50 cm | 648.0 to 666.0 pt | Figures exceeding this vertical envelope are pushed to subsequent pages, creating white-space voids2. |

### **Typographic Hierarchy**

Figure text should use sans-serif typefaces (Helvetica, Arial, or TeX Gyre Heros) to maintain legibility at high resolutions3. Text sizes within figures must balance document harmony and readability when rendered at 100% scale in the final PDF:

* **Sub-panel Identifiers** ((a), (b), (c)): 8.5 pt to 9.0 pt, bold sans-serif.  
* **Axis Titles and Measurement Units**: 8.0 pt to 8.5 pt, bold sans-serif.  
* **Category Names and Tick Labels**: 7.0 pt to 7.5 pt, regular sans-serif.  
* **In-chart Annotations and Legends**: 6.0 pt to 6.5 pt, regular sans-serif.  
* **Minimum Legibility Floor**: 5.5 pt. Text smaller than 5.5 pt becomes illegible in print and will draw criticism from reviewers.

### **Color-Blind Safe Palettes**

ACM publications require figures to be accessible to readers with color-vision deficiencies and legible when printed in grayscale3. Traditional red-green color maps (jet, rainbow) should be avoided. The following palettes are recommended:

* **Color Universal Design (Okabe-Ito)**: Designed for discrete experimental traces, baseline comparisons, and categorical bars4. Hexadecimal values:  
  * Black: \#000000  
  * Orange: \#E69F00  
  * Sky Blue: \#56B4E9  
  * Bluish Green: \#009E73  
  * Yellow: \#F0E442  
  * Blue: \#0072B2  
  * Vermillion: \#D55E00  
  * Red-Purple: \#CC79A7  
    \[cite: 4, 6\]  
    This palette maintains clear luminance and chromatic contrast across deutan, protan, and tritan vision profiles, as well as in grayscale conversions3.  
* **Viridis Colormap**: Ideal for 2D acoustic spectrograms, continuous latency surfaces, and power heatmaps. It monotonically increases in luminance, preserving data trends across printing modes.  
* **Cividis Colormap**: Optimized specifically for color-vision deficiencies, making it an excellent alternative for high-density confusion matrices and sensitivity sweeps.

### **Vector Graphics Export and TAPS Pipeline Validation**

To ensure clean rendering on high-DPI displays and prevent rasterization blur, figures must be exported as pure vector graphics:

> 1. **Export Formats**: Figures should be generated as Portable Document Format (**PDF**) or Encapsulated PostScript (**EPS**) files3. Raster formats (**PNG**, **JPEG**) are unacceptable for line plots, bar charts, and confusion matrices.  
> 2. **Font Embedding**: Fonts must be embedded as Type 42 (TrueType) or Type 1 vector glyphs to prevent substitution errors during ACM TAPS processing11. In Python Matplotlib scripts, set font embedding explicitly:  
>    Python  
>    import matplotlib  
>    matplotlib.rcParams\['pdf.fonttype'\] \= 42  
>    matplotlib.rcParams\['ps.fonttype'\] \= 42

> 3. **Bounding-Box Cropping**: Use bbox\_inches='tight' and pad\_inches=0.02 to remove excess whitespace around plots, ensuring figures fit snugly into columns without manual LaTeX adjustments.

## **Visual Patterns and Caption Strategies in Premier Systems Papers**

Data presentation in top-tier ACM SenSys, IEEE/ACM IPSN, and ACM MobiSys papers exhibits key structural and stylistic differences compared to rejected manuscripts14.

### **Effective Visual Design Patterns**

Top-tier systems papers consistently apply several visual design patterns:

* **In-Figure Key Takeaway Annotations**: Rather than forcing reviewers to find quantitative results in the text, top papers place key findings directly inside figures. Using callout arrows to highlight takeaways—such as pointing to a knee point labeled *"6.4× energy reduction via PIO sleep gating"*—makes core contributions immediately visible.  
* **Integrated Hardware-Software Evaluation Panels**: Strong papers pair algorithmic detection curves directly with physical power measurements. Placing a DET curve in sub-panel (a) next to an energy waterfall in sub-panel (b) provides a complete picture of the accuracy-energy tradeoff.  
* **Directly Labeled Curves**: Rather than relying on large, detached legends that require constant cross-referencing, strong figures label traces directly at their terminal points or along the curves.

### **Standalone LaTeX PGFPlots Waterfall Implementation**

The following LaTeX PGFPlots code generates an energy waterfall figure sized for an ACM single column (3.33 inches / 8.45 cm)2:

Code snippet  
\\documentclass\[tikz,border=2pt\]{standalone}  
\\usepackage{pgfplots}  
\\pgfplotsset{compat=1.18}  
\\usepackage{helvet}  
\\usepackage\[eulergreek\]{sansmath}

\\begin{document}  
\\begin{tikzpicture}  
\\begin{axis}\[  
    sansmath,  
    font=\\sffamily\\footnotesize,  
    width=8.45cm,  
    height=4.8cm,  
    ybar stacked,  
    bar width=14pt,  
    ymin=0, ymax=28,  
    ylabel={Power Consumption \[mW\]},  
    ylabel style={font=\\sffamily\\bfseries\\scriptsize, yshift=-4pt},  
    symbolic x coords={Continuous, SoftwareVAD, PIONet\_S1, PIONet\_Full},  
    xtick=data,  
    xticklabels={  
        {Continuous CPU},  
        {WebRTC VAD},  
        {PIO Stage-1},  
        {PIO-Net (Full)}  
    },  
    x tick label style={font=\\sffamily\\scriptsize, rotate=15, anchor=north east},  
    ymajorgrids=true,  
    grid style={dashed, gray\!30},  
    legend style={  
        font=\\sffamily\\tiny,  
        at={(0.5, 1.05)},  
        anchor=south,  
        legend columns=3,  
        draw=none,  
        fill=none  
    }  
\]

% Category 1: Static Quiescent / Sleep Floor (Gray)  
\\addplot+\[ybar, fill=gray\!40, draw=gray\!70\] coordinates {  
    (Continuous, 1.2) (SoftwareVAD, 1.2) (PIONet\_S1, 1.2) (PIONet\_Full, 1.2)

    at (axis cs:PIONet\_Full, 3.65) {};

\\end{axis}

### **Self-Contained Figure Captions**

Captions in top-tier ACM publications should be self-contained: a reviewer reading only the figures and captions should easily understand the experimental methodology, baseline comparisons, and core results11. Effective captions follow a clear three-part structure:

> 1. **Core Takeaway in Bold**: A direct opening statement summarizing the primary finding.  
> 2. **Context and Experimental Conditions**: The test setup, baseline configurations, datasets, and operational parameters.  
> 3. **Key Quantitative Result**: The primary numerical trade-off or performance metric shown in the figure.

#### **Example Caption 1: Detection Error Tradeoff Evaluation**

**Figure 4: PIO-Net Keyword Detection Performance Under Acoustic Noise.** Detection Error Tradeoff (DET) curves compare the two-stage PIO-Net pipeline against standalone continuous DSCNNMicro execution, WebRTC software VAD cascading, and an analog comparator baseline across three test environments: Quiet Office (+20 dB SNR), Ambient Babble (+10 dB SNR), and Industrial Factory (0 dB SNR). The x-axis shows the False Alarm Probability (![][image17], bottom) alongside calibrated False Wakes per Hour (FW/hr, top), computed for a 1.0-second sliding inference window stride. The y-axis shows the False Rejection Rate (![][image16]) plotted on a normal deviate (probit) scale5. Hollow markers identify the selected deployment threshold (![][image65]). PIO-Net achieves 0.28 False Wakes/hour at a 4.8% Miss Rate in office environments, matching the accuracy of continuous Cortex-M0+ processing while reducing active CPU duty cycles by 96.2%.

#### **Example Caption 2: Energy Waterfall and Battery Lifetime**

**Figure 7: Cascaded Power Consumption Breakdown and Projected Battery Lifetimes.** (a) Power waterfall comparing baseline continuous INT8 DSCNNMicro execution on the RP2040 (125 MHz) against WebRTC VAD polling and the PIO-Net two-stage hardware pipeline. Offloading the 1-bit PDM popcount filter to the PIO state machine allows Core 0 to remain clock-gated in sleep mode during Stage 1, reducing continuous monitoring power from 23.5 mW to 3.2 mW7. (b) Projected battery lifetime as a function of acoustic trigger frequency across three representative portable power sources: a CR2032 coin cell (225 mAh, derated to 170 mAh), 2x AAA alkaline batteries (1000 mAh), and a 500 mAh LiPo cell. At an average trigger rate of 20 wake events per hour, PIO-Net achieves an estimated operational lifetime of 3.8 months on a single CR2032 coin cell, a 5.9× improvement over conventional software-polled VAD approaches.

## **Production Checklist for Camera-Ready Finalization**

* Confirm all single-column figures measure exactly 3.33 inches (8.45 cm) and full-width spanning figures measure 7.00 inches (17.78 cm)2. Ensure no graphical marks or labels extend into the 0.33-inch column gutter2.  
* Verify that all figure text uses sans-serif typefaces (Helvetica, Arial, or TeX Gyre Heros)3. Ensure labels render between 6.0 pt and 8.5 pt at 100% scale, with no text falling below the 5.5 pt legibility floor.  
* Confirm that Detection Error Tradeoff (DET) plots include a secondary horizontal axis calibrating False Alarm Probability (![][image17]) to False Wakes per Hour (FW/hr) based on the sliding window stride.  
* Print the manuscript on a monochrome laser printer (or inspect in grayscale) to ensure that all line styles, markers, and confusion matrix cells remain distinct without color3.  
* Run pdffonts \<manuscript\>.pdf on the final compiled camera-ready PDF. Confirm that all fonts are identified as Type 1 or TrueType and that no unbound Type 3 bitmapped fonts are present, ensuring smooth validation in the ACM TAPS pipeline11.
